of task mice (Fig. 4), and locomotion-dependent modulation throughout. The ordering we
obtain (position ≈ stimulus > licking > speed) matches that picture: position and
texture identity are the two variables the paper shows to be most strongly and most
widely encoded, whereas the lick signal is reported only for the task cohort (28 of
89 sessions) and instantaneous running speed is the noisiest of the four.

### Check 3 — train vs validation gap
| Output | Train | Validation | Train/Val |
|---|---|---|---|
| stimulus | 0.998 | 0.861 | 1.16 |
| licking | 0.991 | 0.773 | 1.28 |
| position_bin | 1.000 | 0.897 | 1.12 |
| speed_bin | 0.940 | 0.574 | **1.64** |

Only `speed_bin` exceeds the 1.5× threshold. **Investigated with an ablation** rather
than assumed: the decoder learns a *separate* `nneurons × 100` projection for every
session — 200,000 parameters per session against ~6,500 training samples per session —
so it can memorise training timepoints. Halving the neuron count halves that capacity:

| neurons/session | speed_bin train | speed_bin validation | train/val |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1000 | 0.779 | 0.575 | 1.35 |
| 1500 | 0.867 | 0.571 | 1.52 |
| 2000 | 0.940 | 0.574 | 1.64 |

The **validation** accuracy is flat at 0.574 ± 0.002 across all three. The extra
training accuracy is therefore pure memorisation of the per-session projection and is a
property of the decoder's capacity, not of the data: if there were label leakage the
validation accuracy would rise with capacity, and if the conversion were misaligned the
validation accuracy would fall towards chance. Neither happens. The same ablation shows
there is no leakage in the other three outputs either (their validation accuracies move
smoothly and by small amounts with capacity).

### Check 4 — choosing the neuron cap (ablation on the full dataset)
Validation balanced accuracy, full 89-session dataset:

| neurons/session | stimulus | licking | position | speed | mean | pickle |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1000 | 0.825 | 0.810 | 0.845 | 0.575 | 0.764 | 3.3 GB |
| 1500 | 0.845 | 0.783 | 0.875 | 0.571 | 0.768 | 4.9 GB |
| **2000** | **0.861** | **0.773** | **0.897** | **0.574** | **0.776** | **6.6 GB** |
| 3000 | 0.278 | 0.708 | 0.578 | 0.332 | 0.474 | 9.8 GB |
| 4000 | 0.287 | 0.705 | 0.551 | 0.334 | 0.469 | 13.1 GB |

2000 (which is also the decoder's own `svd_max_neurons`) is the best choice and was
kept. The collapse at ≥3000 is an optimisation failure of the *provided* decoder, not a
data problem: its L1 penalty `1e-4 · Σ|W|` grows with the neuron count while the
per-weight data gradient shrinks, so beyond ~2000 neurons the penalty drives the
projection to zero (train and validation accuracy collapse *together*, the signature of
under-fitting rather than over-fitting). Two independent runs at 2000 neurons gave
0.860/0.760/0.896/0.573 and 0.863/0.750/0.893/0.574, so the operating point is stable,
and the 1000 → 1500 → 2000 trend is smooth.

### Check 5 — z-scoring ablation
| neural scaling | stimulus | licking | position | speed | mean |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| per-neuron z-score (kept) | 0.861 | 0.773 | 0.897 | 0.574 | 0.776 |
| raw deconvolved amplitudes | 0.826 | 0.780 | 0.870 | 0.630 | 0.777 |

Accuracy is a wash (0.776 vs 0.777), so the choice was made on principle, not on the
metric: z-scoring is what the reference code does before any population read-out
(`stats.zscore(spk, axis=1)` in `get_kfold_reward_response` and `Get_sort_spk`), it puts

dataset insensitive to the decoder's input scaling. `convert_data.py --no-zscore`
reproduces the ablation.

### Issues found and resolved in this step
- None new. The two issues found earlier (the plotting overlap and the corridor/grey
  boundary artifact) are documented in Step 10 and were fixed before this step.

---

## Step 13: Documentation and Cleanup
**Status**: COMPLETE

- [x] `README.md` created (dataset description, how to load, format spec, key statistics)
- [x] `cache/` folder created with the investigation scripts and `README_CACHE.md`
- [x] All files organised

### Final file inventory
| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `convert_data.py` | the conversion script |
| `converted_data.pkl` | full converted dataset (6.57 GB, 89 sessions) |
| `sample_data.pkl` | 2-session sample (0.09 GB) |
| `CONVERSION_NOTES.md` | this file |
| `README.md` | user-facing summary |
| `conversion_sample_out.txt`, `verification_sample_out.txt`, `train_decoder_sample_out.txt` | sample run logs |
| `conversion_full_out.txt`, `verification_full_out.txt`, `train_decoder_full_out.txt` | full run logs |
| `processing_*.png` | per-step processing figures for 2 sessions |
| `sample_trials.png`, `predictions.png` | decoder-harness figures |
| `cache/` | independent sanity-check script and exploration notes |
'''
open(p,'w').write(s[:s.index('## Step 10: Critical Review 1')] + new)
print('written')

# Zhong et al. 2025 visual-cortex VR dataset — decoder-ready conversion

Converted form of the two-photon mesoscope dataset from

> Zhong, Baptista, Gattoni, Arnold, Flickinger, Stringer & Pachitariu,
> **"Unsupervised pretraining in biological neural networks"**, *Nature* **644**, 741 (2025).
> Data: figshare item 28811129. Code: `zhong-et-al-2025`.

`converted_data.pkl` holds every one of the paper's 89 recordings in the standard
`{neural, input, output, …}` decoder format, temporally aligned to corridor entry.

---

## The experiment in one paragraph

Head-fixed mice run on a ball through 4 m linear virtual-reality corridors whose walls
carry "frozen" crops of naturalistic textures (circle/leaf for most mice, rock/wood for
some), separated by 2 m of grey space. The VR advances at a constant 60 cm s⁻¹ whenever
the mouse runs faster than 6 cm s⁻¹ and is frozen otherwise. A sound cue is played at a
position drawn uniformly from 0.5–3.5 m on every trial. In the **task** cohort (28 of
89 sessions) the cue marks the start of the reward zone in one of the two corridors and
licking after it delivers water; **unsupervised** and **naive** mice see the same
corridors and hear the same cue but are never rewarded. Neural activity is Suite2p
non-negative deconvolved calcium (τ = 0.75 s) from V1 and higher visual areas, sampled
at 3.176 Hz.

---

## Loading

```python
import pickle
with open('/app/converted_data.pkl', 'rb') as f:
    data = pickle.load(f)

data['neural'][s][t]            # (2000, T) float32, z-scored deconvolved activity
data['input'][s][t]             # (4, T)    float32
data['output'][s][t]            # (4, T)    int64, class indices
data['subjects'][data['subject_idx'][s]]      # mouse name for session s
data['brain_regions'][data['brain_region_idx'][s][n]]  # area of neuron n in session s
data['metadata']['session_info'][s]           # provenance for session s
```

Sessions are ordered by (mouse, date, block); `metadata['session_info'][s]['session']`
gives the original `<mname>_<datexp>_<blk>` key.

## Format specification

### `neural`
89 sessions × (84–722 trials) × `(2000, T)` float32. `T` is the number of imaging
frames the animal spent running inside the 0–4 m texture region on that trial
(median 21, mean 21.6, range 11–178). One time bin = one imaging frame = **314.85 ms**.

### `input` — decoder inputs, `(4, T)` float32
| # | name | type | description |
|---|------|------|-------------|
| 0 | `time_to_sound_cue_s` | continuous, time-varying | signed seconds until the sound cue (positive before it, 0 at the cue, negative after) |
| 1 | `day_of_training` | continuous, per-trial | days since that mouse's first imaging session (0–92) |
| 2 | `time_since_trial_start_s` | continuous, time-varying | seconds of running since corridor entry |
| 3 | `reward_available` | binary, per-trial | 1 if this corridor is the rewarded one, else 0 |

Per-trial inputs are broadcast across the `T` columns. Times 0 and 2 are measured on the
"running clock" — elapsed time accumulated over running frames only, because
non-running samples are excluded from the dataset (see `CONVERSION_NOTES.md`, Step 5).

### `output` — variables to decode, `(4, T)` int64
| # | name | classes | `output_values` |
|---|------|---------|-----------------|
| 0 | `stimulus` | 7 | `circle1, circle2, leaf1, leaf2, leaf3, leaf1_swap1, leaf1_swap2` |
| 1 | `licking` | 2 | `no_lick, lick` — ≥1 lick in this time bin |
| 2 | `position_bin` | 4 | `0-1m, 1-2m, 2-3m, 3-4m` |
| 3 | `speed_bin` | 4 | `speed_q1 … speed_q4` — quartiles of running speed over the whole dataset (edges 12.40, 25.28, 40.75 cm s⁻¹) |

`stimulus` uses the paper's own `stim_id` code, which is **role-based**, not name-based:
`leaf1` is always the exemplar that plays the rewarded role, so labels are comparable
across mice that were shown different texture sets (circle/leaf vs rock/wood).

### `metadata`
`task_description`, `time_bin_size` (314.85 ms), `temporal_alignment_event`
("trial start = entry into the visual corridor"), `off_start` (0.0), `off_end` (`None`,
trials have variable length), plus `sample_selection`, `neuron_selection`,
`trial_selection`, `time_base`, `speed_bin_edges`, `sampling_rate_hz`, and
`session_info` — a per-session record with mouse, date, block, cohort, reward mode,
rewarded wall, day of training, trial counts, neuron counts and frame interval.

---

## Key statistics

| | |
|---|---|
| Sessions | 89 (matches the paper's "89 recordings") |
| Mice | 19 (1–8 sessions each) |
| Trials | 37,801 (84–722 per session, median 429) |
| Timepoints | 815,485 |
| Neurons recorded | 20,547–89,577 per session (the paper's exact range), 4,691,034 total |
| Neurons in visual cortex | 4,105,393 |
| Neurons kept | 2,000 per session = 178,000 (V1 78,082 · mHV 50,617 · lHV 20,720 · aHV 28,581) |
| Cohorts | 28 task, 46 unsupervised, 15 naive/grating-control sessions |
| Output fractions | stimulus (.319, .060, .335, .170, .059, .027, .029) · licking (.963, .037) · position (.250, .249, .250, .252) · speed (.25, .25, .25, .25) |

### Curation applied
- samples: inside the 0–4 m texture region **and** the VR moving (`ft_CorrSpc &
  ft_move > 0`) — the paper's own analysis window;
- neurons: inside visual cortex (`iarea ∉ {−1, 7}`), non-zero variance, then a
  region-stratified random subsample of 2,000 per session (a full-resolution dataset
  would be 151.5 GB and is not trainable in practice — see `CONVERSION_NOTES.md`);
- trials: 309 `circle3` trials (0.81 %, 4 sessions) dropped — the reference assigns them
  no stimulus role; 21 boundary samples dropped where `ft_Pos` had already wrapped to
  the next corridor.

---

## Decoder performance

`python /app/train_decoder.py /app/converted_data.pkl`

| Output | Chance | Train balanced acc | **Validation balanced acc** |
|---|---|---|---|
| stimulus | 0.143 | 0.998 | **0.861** |
| licking | 0.500 | 0.991 | **0.773** |
| position_bin | 0.250 | 1.000 | **0.897** |
| speed_bin | 0.250 | 0.940 | **0.574** |

## Reproducing

```bash
python -u /app/convert_data.py /app/converted_data.pkl --full --workers 8   # ~60 s
python -u /app/convert_data.py /app/sample_data.pkl --sample --show-processing
python -u /app/train_decoder.py /app/converted_data.pkl --plot-samples      # ~5 min on an L4
python -u /app/cache/sanity_checks.py                                       # independent checks
```

Options: `--max-neurons N` (default 2000), `--no-zscore` (ablation),
`--workers K`, `--show-processing` (per-step figures for 2 sessions).

Full rationale for every decision, all validation results, and the ablations behind the
2,000-neuron cap and the z-scoring choice are in `CONVERSION_NOTES.md`.

# cache/ — investigation and validation artefacts

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `sanity_checks.py` | **Independent** verification of `../converted_data.pkl`. Re-reads the original `/app/data` files and re-derives the retained-sample mask, the z-scored neural matrix, and all four inputs and outputs from scratch (it does *not* import `convert_data.py`), then compares with `np.allclose` / `np.array_equal`. Also checks the dataset-level statistics against the paper. Run with `python /app/cache/sanity_checks.py`; exits non-zero if any check fails. Current status: **0 of 41 checks fail**. | `ablation_neurons_1000.txt`, `..._1500.txt`, `..._3000.txt`, `..._4000.txt` | Full-dataset decoder runs at other values of `--max-neurons`, used to choose the 2000-neuron cap (CONVERSION_NOTES Step 12, Check 4). |
| `ablation_neurons_1000_4000_summary.txt` | Combined stdout of the 1000 / 4000 sweep. |
| `ablation_no_zscore.txt` | Full-dataset decoder run on data converted with `--no-zscore` (CONVERSION_NOTES Step 12, Check 5). |
| `train_2000_repeat2.txt` | A second training run at the chosen setting, used to measure run-to-run variability (±0.01 balanced accuracy). |

after each run; `convert_data.py --max-neurons N [--no-zscore]` regenerates them.
EOF

All 13 steps are complete. Summary of what was built and verified:

## Conversion

**Source → target.** 89 recordings (19 mice) of Suite2p-deconvolved mesoscope activity from V1 + higher visual areas, with mice running VR corridors. The 142 `Imaging_Exp_info` records collapse to 89 unique recordings (verified identical behaviour payloads; only `stim_id` labelling differs, so it is merged).

**Key decisions, all traced to the reference:**
- **Samples** = inside the 0–4 m texture region **and** VR moving — exactly `utils.Get_dprime_selective_neuron`'s `fr_valid = VRmove & isCorridor`, verified numerically identical frame-for-frame, and the paper's stated analysis window.
- **Alignment** = corridor entry, native imaging frames (314.85 ms), no positional interpolation.
- **Neurons** = visual cortex only (`iarea ∉ {−1,7}`, the reference's rule), z-scored, then a region-stratified 2,000/session subsample. Keeping all 4.1 M neurons would be a 151.5 GB array that the provided decoder cannot train on; 2,000 is also its own `svd_max_neurons`.
- **Stimulus output** = the paper's role-based `stim_id` (7 classes), which is what makes labels comparable across mice shown circle/leaf vs rock/wood.
- **Time inputs** on a "running clock", because wall-clock trial duration has a tail to 1,765 s produced entirely by the stops the paper excludes.

## Verification
- **41 independent sanity checks pass** (`cache/sanity_checks.py`, written against the raw files, not the conversion code): random neurons/trials match the raw z-scored `spk` to 1e-4 including their area labels; all four inputs and outputs match an independent recomputation for every trial of 7 sessions.
- Paper statistics reproduced exactly: 89 recordings, 19 mice, **20,547–89,577 neurons per recording**, 4 m/60 cm s⁻¹ ⇒ predicted 21.2 samples/trial vs 21 observed.
- **Two bugs found and fixed**: a plotting overlap that hid the reward trace (data was correct), and a real boundary artifact where 21 trials picked up a sample whose position had already wrapped into the *next* corridor.

## Decoder (full dataset, validation balanced accuracy)

| Output | Chance | Val acc | ×chance |
|---|---|---|---|
| stimulus (7) | 0.143 | **0.861** | 6.0 |
| licking (2) | 0.500 | **0.773** | 1.55 |
| position_bin (4) | 0.250 | **0.897** | 3.6 |
| speed_bin (4) | 0.250 | **0.574** | 2.3 |

Two caveats worth flagging: the paper reports **no** decoding accuracies anywhere, so there is no published number to compare against — the comparison table in Step 12 is necessarily empty. And `speed_bin`'s train/val gap is 1.64×; an ablation shows validation accuracy is flat at 0.574 across 1000/1500/2000 neurons while training accuracy climbs from 0.78 to 0.94, so the gap is the decoder's per-session projection memorising, not leakage in the data.
